Power series rings

Source: R/polys-series-ring.R
power_series_ring.Rd

A port of SymPy's sympy.polys.series: power_series_ring(symbol, K, prec) returns the ring of power series in one variable over ZZ or QQ truncated at O(x^prec), together with its generator, as list(R, x). Series are added, multiplied, divided and raised to integer powers with the usual operators; an exact polynomial has no O() term until it grows past the ring precision. The ring R holds the methods of SymPy's ring as functions: R$compose(s, t), R$inverse(s), R$reversion(s), R$differentiate(s), R$truncate(s, n), R$square(s), R$from_list(coeffs, prec), R$from_expr(e), R$to_list(s), R$to_expr(s) and R$order_term(); over QQ also R$integrate(), R$sqrt(), R$log(), R$log1p(), R$exp(), R$expm1(), R$sin(), R$cos(), R$tan(), R$sinh(), R$cosh(), R$tanh(), R$asin(), R$asinh(), R$atan(), R$atanh() and R$hypot(). PowerSeriesRingRing() and PowerSeriesRingField() build the rings over ZZ and QQ directly.

Usage

power_series_ring(symbol, K, prec = 6)

PowerSeriesRingRing(domain = ZZ, symbol = "x", prec = 6)

PowerSeriesRingField(domain = QQ, symbol = "x", prec = 6)

Arguments

symbol

The variable name, or a symbol.

K

The ground domain, ZZ or QQ.

prec

The ring precision.

domain

The ground domain.

Value

power_series_ring() a list of the ring and its generator; the other constructors a ring.

Examples

r <- power_series_ring("x", QQ, 6)
R <- r[[1]]; x <- r[[2]]
(1 + x + x^2)^3
#> 1 + 3*x + 6*x^2 + 7*x^3 + 6*x^4 + 3*x^5 + O(x^6) 
R$sin(x)
#> x - 1/6*x^3 + 1/120*x^5 + O(x^6) 
R$compose(R$exp(x) - 1, x + x^2)
#> x + 3/2*x^2 + 7/6*x^3 + 25/24*x^4 + 27/40*x^5 + O(x^6) 
R$reversion(R$sin(x))
#> x + 1/6*x^3 + 3/40*x^5 + O(x^6) 
R$to_expr(R$tan(x))
#> x + x^3/3 + 2*x^5/15 + O(x^6)
